anomaly_def.Name: Schema and Index Design Anomaly + Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Schema and Index Design Anomaly : Physical table, index, partition, or datatype choices mismatch workload access patterns, forcing inefficient access paths even when queries are well written.
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Catalogued statistics no longer reflect true data distribution, causing systematic cardinality misestimates and poor plan selection.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : On-disk pages or index structures are physically or logically corrupt, producing inconsistent or missing rows and forcing plan fall-backs.

When these three root causes coexist, the database exhibits a convoluted mix of symptoms: queries swing unpredictably between full scans caused by bad schema design and emergency scans forced by index corruption; estimated versus actual row counts diverge wildly, yet re-gathering statistics yields unstable or non-deterministic plans because corrupt or poorly designed indexes supply misleading sampling data; repeated recompilations, sudden plan switches, lock escalation, and erratic latency spikes occur. Maintenance operations such as index rebuilds or statistics collection may abort with integrity errors, while write operations suffer from both oversized, non-covering, and possibly corrupted indexes, inflating I/O, blocking, and recovery times. Troubleshooting becomes difficult because each anomaly masks or mimics the symptoms of the others—for example, missing rows might stem from either bad join plans, poor schema alignment, or physical corruption.

Causal interaction: a flawed schema and index design increases index size, depth, and page churn, which in turn raises the likelihood of physical page or linkage corruption. Corrupted or bloated indexes distort sampling and histogram creation, making statistics rapidly inaccurate; conversely, stale or coarse statistics obscure the need for design fixes and can direct the optimizer to rely on damaged indexes, amplifying data-corruption symptoms. Together, the three anomalies form a feedback loop: design flaws create stress and complexity, corruption degrades the very structures relied on to compensate for design gaps, and statistics mislead the optimizer into repeatedly choosing the worst possible paths, driving up load, I/O, and failure probability across both OLTP and analytical workloads.

entry.official_definition: The time limit for regular expression matching operations performed by the regular expression engine.
entry.trigger_condition: A regular expression match operation exceeds regexp_time_limit.
entry.workload_impact: The regular expression operation is constrained by the configured time limit.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when statement execution exceeds a configured execution-time budget because the operation runs too long or the workload is blocked behind other work.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect query shape, access path quality, resource contention, and whether the timeout threshold should be reviewed together with the workload pattern.
